q2: SELECT DISTINCT EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) > 1

q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) > 1
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 returns duplicate email values (but only one per group due to GROUP BY), while Q2 returns distinct email values. However, in practice, both queries return one row per distinct email due to GROUP BY, so the difference is subtle. The DISTINCT in Q2 is redundant but harmless. However, in some SQL dialects, using SELECT with GROUP BY and no aggregate without DISTINCT may produce unexpected results when combined with HAVING, but in standard SQL, both queries are effectively the same.
counterexample_dsp: In practice, both queries yield the same result under standard SQL semantics. However, if there is a misunderstanding, no meaningful counterexample exists because GROUP BY on EMAIL ensures one row per email value.
